selection_guide: Pick the component that carries a single claim best for a given recipient and target info-depth (L1 sparse hooks .. L4 dense doc-body). Reason in three passes. (1) CLAIM-SHAPE: what is the content's essential shape? A number that is the point -> metric family (metric-tiles, stat-row); a part-of-whole split -> proportion-bars or a pie chart; a before/after -> cmp-table or transform-grid; an option decision -> option-grid; a time/step order -> beat-list or flow-steps or phase-row; a flat set of peers -> card-set (2-5), two-column-list/tag-wall (10-40); a feature yes/no grid -> matrix; a wide raw dataset -> dense-table or pipeline-table; a quote -> pull-quote or statement; a bottom-line verdict -> verdict-callout/ask-box; a network/architecture -> arch-diagram/flow-embed; rigor/sourcing -> evidence-list/bias-check/provenance. Match the content's shape to the entry whose `carries` lists it. (2) INFO-DEPTH: L1 wants one focal hook that lands in 3 seconds (statement, statement-title, one big metric, a pull-quote) -> pick sparse, focal entries and show fewer items; L2 wants a scannable primary block (card-set, option-grid, proportion-bars, beat-list); L3 wants dense evidence the reader will study (dense-table, matrix, evidence-list, pipeline-table, prose); L4 is full doc body (prose, dense-table). Prefer entries whose `info_depths` include the target level, and lower an item count before overflowing a sparse component. (3) RECIPIENT: an executive/board recipient -> lead with verdict/metric/ask components and hide detail behind disclosure-list or provenance; a technical/analyst recipient -> matrix, dense-table, pipeline-table, evidence-list carry the rigor they expect; a mixed audience -> lens-reframe restates one claim per persona, persona-row names who is in the room. CAPACITY is a hard filter, never a preference: if the claim has more items than a component's `capacity.max`, either drop to a higher-capacity component of the same shape (card-set 5 -> two-column-list 24 -> tag-wall 40 for a growing set) or render a truthful subset and surface the remainder elsewhere. Never trade semantic fit for raw capacity (a 5-item set never lands on a comparison matrix just because it holds more). ANTI-SAMENESS: avoid two blocks that paint identically (the card-grid family: card-set, verb-grid, story-grid, transform-grid, metric-tiles, option-grid) on one slide — a grid beside a table/list reads as intentional hierarchy; two grids read as one mismatched block. Every block can carry a `provenance` affordance; add it whenever the recipient will ask 'says who?'.

entries.name: Statement Title
entries.one_liner: The single display-type headline that names the ONE claim of a slide (<=22ch).
entries.when_to_use: Use as the slide's title: one short, declarative claim in large type that every other block on the slide supports. Best when you can compress the point to <=22 characters and want it to read as the anchor. Carries narrative framing and can double as a soft verdict header.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for the cover/hook of a whole deck (use `statement`), for body sentences (use `lede` or `prose`), or when the claim needs more than ~22ch — it will truncate or shrink awkwardly.

entries.name: Lede
entries.one_liner: A one-sentence supporting frame set under a title (<=70ch).
entries.when_to_use: Use directly beneath a title to add the one sentence of context or framing the headline cannot hold — the 'why this matters' line. Pure narrative connective tissue at L1/L2.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid when the supporting content is more than one sentence (use `prose`), or when it carries data/structure rather than framing — a lede is prose-only, no items.

entries.name: Prose
entries.one_liner: Full markdown typography — the L3/L4 document body block.
entries.when_to_use: Use for genuine prose: multi-sentence explanation, argument, or narrative that needs headings, lists, emphasis, or an inline blockquote. The universal fallback when a claim has no cleaner structural shape. Reflows freely and can carry provenance. Also holds a quote acceptably (fit 0.7) when a dedicated pull-quote is too loud.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid at L1 (too dense for a hook) and whenever the content has a crisp shape a purpose-built component renders better — a set, comparison, metric, or sequence should not be buried in paragraphs.

entries.name: Disclosure List
entries.one_liner: Expandable evidence rows: mark + title + sub, with a reveal body underneath.
entries.when_to_use: Use for a set of 3-7 findings/items where each has a headline the reader scans plus detail they can expand on demand — progressive disclosure. Ideal for an exec audience: the titles carry the summary, the reveal bodies hold the proof. Supports a per-row severity mark. Carries sets, narrative findings, and verdicts, and can hold quotes.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid when items have no expandable detail (use `card-set` or `two-column-list`), when there are more than 7 (use `dense-table`/`two-column-list`), or when the reader needs everything visible at once.

entries.name: Card Set
entries.one_liner: Auto-fit grid of 2-5 content cards (eyebrow/title/body/footer).
entries.when_to_use: Use for a flat set of 2-5 peer items that each deserve a titled card with a short body — features, pillars, workstreams, options without a decision. The default 'a handful of related things' block. Also carries a light metric or loose comparison.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid past 5 items (overflows — use `two-column-list` or `tag-wall`), when one option should be recommended (use `option-grid`), or when a second card-grid already sits on the slide (anti-sameness — switch to a list/table).

entries.name: Metric Tiles
entries.one_liner: 2-4 KPI tiles (label/value/desc) where the number is the point.
entries.when_to_use: Use when 2-4 headline numbers ARE the message — KPIs, results, magnitudes the recipient should remember. Value renders large and focal. Best for an exec/board L1-L2 hook. Also carries a delta framing and a light proportion.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for a single number (use `stat-row` or a `statement`), for more than 4 metrics (use `stat-row` up to 4 or a `chart`), or when the number needs a trend/time axis (use `chart`).

entries.name: Callout
entries.one_liner: Left-accent-bar emphasis box in note/info/warn tone.
entries.when_to_use: Use to lift ONE short passage out of the flow — a caveat, a key insight, a warning — with a tone (accent/info/warn) that signals how to read it. Narrative emphasis, one box only. Pairs well as an aside beside a denser primary block.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for multiple parallel notes (it holds one box), for the main claim itself (use a title/statement), or for structured data.

entries.name: Option Grid
entries.one_liner: Decision matrix of 3-5 option cards with k-v lines, one flagged recommended.
entries.when_to_use: Use for an explicit choose-between decision: 3-5 options, each with the same key/value attributes for side-by-side compare, and exactly one marked recommended. The go-to when the deliverable is a recommendation the recipient must approve. Strongest comparison component and carries a delta between options.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid when no option is recommended (use `card-set` or `matrix`), for yes/no feature grids (use `matrix`), or for more than 5 options.

entries.name: Beat List
entries.one_liner: Time-ordered scenario beats: T-mark + body + actor.
entries.when_to_use: Use for a chronological walkthrough — an incident timeline, a scenario, a demo narrative — where each beat has a time/marker, what happens, and who acts. 3-10 beats. Carries sequence primarily and light relationship (actor-to-action).
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for numbered process steps with tools (use `flow-steps`), for a coarse roadmap of phases (use `phase-row`), or for non-temporal sets.

entries.name: Stat Row
entries.one_liner: Joined horizontal KPI strip: 2-4 num + label cells with tone.
entries.when_to_use: Use for 2-4 numbers presented as a single tight banner strip — a results bar, a headline-metrics ribbon. More compact and unified than metric-tiles; the number leads, tone modifiers color good/bad. A strong L1 focal hook.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid past 4 cells, when each metric needs its own descriptive body (use `metric-tiles`), or when a trend/axis is implied (use `chart`).

entries.name: Persona Row
entries.one_liner: Audience roster pills: mark + name + lens.
entries.when_to_use: Use to name who is in the room / who the deck addresses — 2-4 audience pills, each with a name and the lens they read through. An orienting, supporting element, often on an opening or lens slide.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid when you actually need to reframe a claim per persona (use `lens-reframe`), or as a primary content block — it is an aside/support roster, not an argument.

entries.name: Lens Reframe
entries.one_liner: Persona tab switcher: the same claim restated per audience.
entries.when_to_use: Use when ONE claim must be told differently to 2-4 audiences and you want them to switch between framings — tabs by persona, each pane reframing the same underlying point (e.g. cost to the CFO, risk to the CISO). Ideal for a mixed-audience recipient. Carries a set of framings, narrative, and a soft comparison.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid when the audiences see genuinely different content (not one reframed claim), or when a static side-by-side is enough (use `option-grid`/`matrix`). Only 2-4 tabs.

entries.name: Story Grid
entries.one_liner: Overview chapter cards (num/title/desc) — a table-of-contents affordance.
entries.when_to_use: Use as an index/agenda: 2-4 numbered chapter cards previewing the sections of a deck or document. An orientation device at the top of a story. Carries a set with light narrative sequencing.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for content cards (use `card-set`), for a strict process (use `flow-steps`), or past 4 chapters.

entries.name: Proportion Bars
entries.one_liner: Horizontal share-of-whole / budget-magnitude bars (label/pct/value/level).
entries.when_to_use: Use for a part-of-whole split of 2-8 shares where each bar's length shows its proportion and a level (safe/caution/danger) colors it — budget allocation, capacity usage, share breakdowns. Strongest proportion component; also reads as a light trend and carries the underlying metric.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for a single percentage (use a `statement`/metric), for a true 2D comparison (use `chart` bar), or past 8 bars (use a `chart` or `dense-table`).

entries.name: Flow Steps
entries.one_liner: Numbered agentic-flow steps (num/what/tool/actor).
entries.when_to_use: Use for an ordered process of 4-8 steps where each step names what happens, the tool used, and the actor (human/agent) — pipelines, agent workflows, procedures. Sequence-first with light relationship (actor per step).
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for a timed scenario (use `beat-list`), for a coarse roadmap (use `phase-row`), for fewer than 4 or more than 8 steps, or when there is no ordering.

entries.name: Pipeline Table
entries.one_liner: Multi-column stage comparison table (e.g. layer/edge/cloud/cost).
entries.when_to_use: Use for a structured multi-column comparison of 2-10 rows across a fixed set of stage/dimension columns — architecture stages, deployment tiers with attributes. A denser, more column-oriented comparison than cmp-table's two-column before/after. Carries comparison and a set.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for a simple before->after (use `cmp-table`), for yes/no feature grids (use `matrix`), or for open-ended raw data of 10-30 rows (use `dense-table`).

entries.name: Verb Grid
entries.one_liner: 3-column tool/verb schema cards (name/desc/params/ack).
entries.when_to_use: Use to document a set of 3-6 tools/verbs/API operations, each as a card with name, description, params, and an ack/return — a capability catalog or MCP tool schema. A specialized card-grid for API-shaped sets.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for generic content cards (use `card-set`), for an endpoint table (use `pipeline-table`/`dense-table`), or when another card-grid is already on the slide (anti-sameness).

entries.name: Comparison Table
entries.one_liner: Before->after comparison table with per-row status tags.
entries.when_to_use: Use for a two-column before/after (or v1/v2, old/new) comparison of 2-12 rows, each tagged with a status showing what changed. The default for 'here is what changed' at row scale. Strongest on delta and comparison together.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for multi-dimension stage tables (use `pipeline-table`), yes/no feature grids (use `matrix`), or a punchy card-style before/after of a few items (use `transform-grid`).

entries.name: Transform Grid
entries.one_liner: Before->after transform cards (before / arrow / after + label).
entries.when_to_use: Use for 2-6 punchy before->after transformations shown as cards with a visual arrow — 'from this, to that' payoffs, migrations, improvements. More visual and fewer items than cmp-table; carries delta and comparison.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid past 6 items or when many rows need tight tabular alignment (use `cmp-table`), or when a second card-grid is present (anti-sameness).

entries.name: Phase Row
entries.one_liner: Roadmap phase chain (done/next/future) with arrows.
entries.when_to_use: Use for a coarse roadmap or maturity chain of 2-7 phases, each stated as done / next / future, connected by arrows. The high-level 'where we are on the path' band. Sequence with a forward trend.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for detailed process steps (use `flow-steps`), a timed scenario (use `beat-list`), or when phases carry sub-content rather than a single state label.

entries.name: Verdict Callout
entries.one_liner: Summary banner stating the bottom line with inline stat dots.
entries.when_to_use: Use to deliver the verdict — a headline conclusion (total/summary) plus up to 5 inline stat dots that back it. The 'so what' banner an exec reads first. Strongest verdict component; also carries the headline metric.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for detailed evidence (use `evidence-list`/`dense-table`), for a call-to-action ask (use `ask-box`), or when there is no single conclusion to state.

entries.name: Ask Box
entries.one_liner: Board-ask call-to-action: title + list of specific asks.
entries.when_to_use: Use for the explicit ask/decision the recipient must act on — a titled box listing 1-6 concrete requests (approve budget, assign owner, sign off). The closing 'what we need from you' block. Verdict/narrative shaped.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for stating a conclusion without a request (use `verdict-callout`), for options to weigh (use `option-grid`), or past ~6 asks.

entries.name: Architecture Diagram
entries.one_liner: Flow boxes colored by health, expressing relationship between parts.
entries.when_to_use: Use to show how 2-5 components/systems relate as connected boxes, each colored by a state/health. The lightweight 'how the parts fit together' schematic. Relationship-first with a light set reading.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for a real saved okuro flow with nodes (use `flow-embed`), for an ordered process (use `flow-steps`), or for more than 5 boxes.

entries.name: Provenance
entries.one_liner: Inline source-ref affordance surfaced on demand under any block.
entries.when_to_use: STRUCTURALLY INLINE — not a standalone content block; attach beneath any block to cite 1-5 sources (source + as_of + url). Add whenever the recipient will ask 'says who?' or the claim needs an audit trail. Every block can carry it. Carries no claim-shape of its own; it is a rigor affordance.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid as a primary block or when a full sourced-claims ledger is needed (use `evidence-list`). Not for narrative content.

entries.name: Evidence List
entries.one_liner: Rigor 'nutrition label': claim + source grade + confidence + as_of.
entries.when_to_use: Use to make sourcing explicit for 2-10 claims, each with a source grade (A-D), a confidence number, and an as_of date. The block that answers 'how solid is each claim?' for a rigorous/technical recipient. Carries verdict (per-claim strength), a set, and comparison across grades.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid when a single citation strip suffices (use `provenance`), for cognitive-bias auditing (use `bias-check`), or for undated narrative claims.

entries.name: Bias Check
entries.one_liner: Rigor block listing cognitive biases + risk level + counter-measure.
entries.when_to_use: Use to pre-empt objections by naming 2-8 cognitive biases that could distort the analysis, each with a risk level and a counter-measure. Signals intellectual honesty to a skeptical/technical recipient. Carries a set with a verdict reading (risk per bias).
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for source grading (use `evidence-list`), for general risks that aren't cognitive biases, or when it would read as defensive filler to the audience.

entries.name: Chart
entries.one_liner: Dependency-free single-hue SVG chart (bar/line/area/pie) + annotations.
entries.when_to_use: Use when data needs a real plotted visual: a trend over time (line/area), a magnitude comparison (bar), or a part-of-whole (pie), 2-16 data points, with optional annotations. The strongest trend component and a strong carrier of proportion, comparison, metric, and delta — reach for it whenever a number has a shape a picture shows better than tiles.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for 1-4 standalone KPIs (use `metric-tiles`/`stat-row`), for labeled share bars with status levels (use `proportion-bars`), or past ~16 points (use `dense-table`).

entries.name: Flow Embed
entries.one_liner: Embeds a saved okuro flow by id in a framed, maximizable panel.
entries.when_to_use: Use to show an actual saved okuro flow (by flow_id) as a live framed panel with a maximize affordance — a real node graph rather than a drawn schematic. Strongest relationship carrier; also reads as sequence. One flow per embed.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid when there is no saved flow to reference (use `arch-diagram` to draw one), for ordered steps (use `flow-steps`), or on a sparse L1 hook slide (it is tall/dense).

entries.name: Statement
entries.one_liner: One assertion in huge type — the L1 hook / cover claim.
entries.when_to_use: Use for maximal impact: a single assertion in the largest type, as a deck cover or a full-slide hook that must land in one glance. Carries narrative, a strong verdict, and a quote-cover. The most focal component in the kit.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid as a slide title with supporting blocks (use `statement-title`), for attributed quotations (use `pull-quote`), or anywhere detail/data belongs — it holds one line only.

entries.name: Pull Quote
entries.one_liner: Pull-quote with attribution and an oversized quotation mark.
entries.when_to_use: Use for a single attributed quotation given room to breathe — a customer voice, an expert endorsement, a telling line from a source. Strongest quote component; also carries narrative. One quote per block.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for an unattributed cover assertion (use `statement`), for a quote inside running text (use `prose` blockquote), or for multiple quotes at once.

entries.name: Matrix
entries.one_liner: Feature comparison grid (yes/no/partial) with a winner-column tint.
entries.when_to_use: Use for a capability/feature comparison: rows of features x columns of options, each cell a yes/no/partial mark, with the winning column tinted. The classic 'us vs them' or feature-matrix. Unbounded rows (typical 6, up to 16+). Strongest comparison carrier with a set and a soft verdict.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for a recommendation with attributes (use `option-grid`), for before/after (use `cmp-table`), or when cells hold free text rather than yes/no marks (use `pipeline-table`/`dense-table`).

entries.name: Dense Table
entries.one_liner: Compact open-ended data table, 10-30 rows, zebra + sticky header.
entries.when_to_use: Use for a genuinely large tabular dataset of 10-30 rows the reader will scan/study — the high-cardinality workhorse that renders a long list without truncation (the 13-principles class). Unbounded. Carries comparison, a set, per-row verdict/status, and a light metric.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for a few rows (use `cmp-table`/`pipeline-table`), for yes/no feature grids (use `matrix`), or on an L1 hook (far too dense).

entries.name: Two-Column List
entries.one_liner: 10-24 short items (title + sub) balanced across two columns.
entries.when_to_use: Use for a medium-large flat set of 8-24 short items with a title and one sub-line each, balanced across two columns — the step up from card-set when a handful becomes a long list. Unbounded. Pure set carrier.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid for 2-5 rich cards (use `card-set`), for 20-40 single-word chips (use `tag-wall`), or for tabular data with columns (use `dense-table`).

entries.name: Tag Wall
entries.one_liner: 10-40 chips as a scannable wall (tech list, capability set, glossary).
entries.when_to_use: Use for a large set of 10-40 short single-label items where the SET's breadth is the point, not each item's detail — a tech stack, capability list, glossary, or coverage wall. Unbounded chips with an optional tone. The overflow target when a set outgrows card-set/two-column-list.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid when each item needs a description (use `two-column-list`/`card-set`), for fewer than ~10 items, or when items carry data/structure.

entries.name: Tier Badge
entries.one_liner: Inline pill classifier chip (a tier/label with tone).
entries.when_to_use: STRUCTURALLY INLINE — a single decorative classifier pill embedded within another block (a card, a title, a table cell) to tag a tier/category. Carries a light verdict/classification only. Not placed on its own.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid as a standalone block, for a status verdict (use `verdict-badge`), or for an HTTP method (use `method-badge`).

entries.name: Verdict Badge
entries.one_liner: Inline status chip (dim tint + ink, AA-contrast) carrying a verdict tone.
entries.when_to_use: STRUCTURALLY INLINE — a single status chip embedded in a row/cell/card to mark a verdict state (pass/fail, ok/risk) with an accessible tint. Carries a light verdict only. Use inside tables and disclosure rows to color status.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid as a standalone block, for a tier/category tag (use `tier-badge`), or for an HTTP method (use `method-badge`).

entries.name: Method Badge
entries.one_liner: Inline monospace HTTP-method chip (GET/POST/...).
entries.when_to_use: STRUCTURALLY INLINE — a single mono chip labeling an HTTP method, embedded in an API/endpoint table or verb card. Purely a typographic label; carries no claim-shape of its own.
entries.avoid_when: Avoid as a standalone block, for a tier tag (use `tier-badge`), or for a status verdict (use `verdict-badge`).
